questionsToConsider: Which product areas should people choose from, and do they match how your team is organised?
Who replies to blocked users, and can they really do it the same day?
Do you want to hear from everyone, or only from signed-in customers?
Will you tell people when their request ships, and how?
guide.howToUseResponses: Answer the blocked requests first, since a workaround often keeps a customer who was about to leave. For everything else, group requests by the problem they describe rather than the feature they name: five different asks can share one cause. Export the responses to CSV and count requests by area and how often people would use them, then email the people who left an address when something ships.
customizeSteps: Rename the product areas to the parts of your product people actually talk about.
Edit the urgent ending to say who will reply and through which channel.
Link the form from your help menu, changelog or in-app feedback button, or embed it on your roadmap page.

faqs.q: What should a feature request form ask?
faqs.a: What the person wants to do, the problem behind it, how they manage today and how much it matters. The problem is the most useful part, because it lets you design the right solution.

faqs.q: How do I prioritise feature requests?
faqs.a: Weigh how many people share the underlying problem, how often they hit it and how badly it blocks them. This form asks for each of those, so you can sort by them after exporting.

faqs.q: Should I reply to every feature request?
faqs.a: Reply quickly to anyone who is blocked, and let everyone else know when something they asked for ships. A short acknowledgement is better than silence.

faqs.q: Can I embed a feature request form in my app?
faqs.a: Yes. Share it as a link from your help menu or embed it on a page on your site after copying it with Use this template.
